The official Microsoft Teams integration roadmap and the informal sales/Slack messaging directly contradict each other on readiness, availability, and security.

**Official roadmap position:**  
- The Teams integration is **under active design and planning**, not in development or release. The release target is **Q4 2026 (v2.11.0, November release)**, with a restricted pilot beginning **October 2026** for selected financial/healthcare accounts. It is not generally available [NL-014#NL-014-S07].  
- The integration requires Azure AD token verification, role-token enforcement, and proper permission mapping; it is explicitly not a simple chat wrapper [NL-014#NL-014-S07].  
- Only the **Slack connector** is currently available as a limited pilot for select customers [NL-014#NL-014-S07].  
- Sales enablement guidance says roadmap dates are targets, not contractual guarantees, and sales reps must not guarantee launch dates [NL-009#NL-009-S08].  
- Management is enforcing sales training to prevent overclaiming Teams readiness because the integration is still in design/planning [NL-016#NL-016-S05].

**Informal sales/Slack claims:**  
- In a customer call, VP Sales Marcus Reed claimed the Teams integration is "basically right around the corner," that a working connector is "almost ready for general release," and that an early access build could be enabled for a July pilot [NL-023#NL-023-S04]. That call is explicitly annotated as a significant sales overclaim versus the official roadmap [NL-023#NL-023-S04].  
- In Slack, Marcus pushed to release a "toy bot" as an "alpha" for Meridian, told a prospect the integration is "basically right around the corner," and proposed a custom hardcoded container [NL-027#NL-027-S04][NL-027#NL-027-S02].  
- Engineering/CTO responses in Slack show the actual demo was a basic webhook with **zero tenant isolation, zero permission mapping, zero SSO, and zero formatting/citation links** — described as a "toy" that would be a production security nightmare [NL-027#NL-027-S03][NL-027#NL-027-S04].  
- The CTO confirmed the team is **not actively writing code** for Teams; it is only slated for design in Q4 2026 [NL-027#NL-027-S03].  
- In a sprint-priority debate, Sales asked to move Teams pilot to August, but the CTO and Product refused, keeping the OCR pipeline as the priority and leaving Teams in design for Q4 [NL-015#NL-015-S06].

**Comparison conclusion:**  
Informal sales and Slack claims portray the Teams integration as nearly complete, deployable in July/August, and safe to pilot. The official roadmap and engineering/CTO positions describe it as a future Q4 2026 design-phase item requiring substantial security work, with no production-ready build currently existing. The informal claims materially overstate the integration’s readiness [NL-014#NL-014-S07][NL-027#NL-027-S03][NL-023#NL-023-S04].
